clue.text: Find fault with hotel vent stuck in awkward position?

indicators.note: one piece is wedged into the middle of the other, as something stuck in a gap

parts.note: the splits is a gymnastic posture with the legs flat out in opposite directions, hardly comfortable
to vent is to give air to something; here the noun for what passes through a vent

explanation.surface: A grumble about a hotel's air vent jammed at an odd angle.
explanation.definitionFit: To split hairs is an idiom for quibbling over trivial distinctions, finding fault where little exists.

clue.text: Something worn with diamonds, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a set of matching clothes
second meaning: one of the four card categories, of which diamonds is an example

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests jewellery worn alongside an outfit; the diamonds are the playing-card kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a matching jacket-and-trousers outfit and each of the four sets in a pack of cards.

clue.text: After a thousand goes, clumsy person produces skating jump

indicators.note: the thousand departs from the word for a clumsy person, leaving the rest

parts.note: a klutz is an awkward, bumbling person, from Yiddish
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: A clumsy skater, after a thousand attempts, finally lands a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: The lutz is a figure-skating jump taken off from the back outside edge, named after skater Alois Lutz.

clue.text: This paste needs salt with a mixture of spices, thanks

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, as is a tar
taken as written
masala is the South Asian term for a spice blend, as in garam masala
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A recipe note: this paste needs seasoning with salt and spices, with thanks to the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like an ingredient, but it is the sailor, giving TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Taramasalata is a Greek dip or spread made from fish roe, a creamy pink paste.

clue.text: The setter will read out passage

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so 'the setter will' is I'll

explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a narrow passage in a church or theatre.

taken as written

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is used

clue.text: Stretch a point, to some extent, for one of the guys

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer lies within its letters

parts.note: the phrase whose consecutive letters hold the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'Stretch', 'a' and the start of 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British for a man or fellow, one of the guys.

clue.text: His earnest carousing may suggest this

definitions.text: His earnest carousing may suggest this

indicators.note: drunken revelry throws the letters of the two words into disorder

parts.note: the two words whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A serious man's enthusiastic drinking may indicate high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a man's earnest revelling suggests jovial vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartiness is boisterous, cheerful enthusiasm, the quality a vigorous drinking session displays.

clue.text: Broadcast Scrapheap Challenge's final run across country

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be scattered

indicators.note: only the closing letter of Challenge is used

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken; its possessive ending just links

explanation.walkthrough: Scrapheap Challenge was a British TV show where teams built machines from scrap; 'Broadcast' looks like part of that TV picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is a cross-country race in which runners follow a trail of scattered paper scraps.

clue.text: Placement of flyers plugging trendy joint

the hip is a ball-and-socket joint
terns are seabirds, so flyers

clue.text: Exhibit gaping hole with little width inside

explanation.definitionFit: To gawp is to stare open-mouthed, so to show a gaping, gormless expression.

clue.text: Predictable contest named after Ferrari icon?

definitions.meaning: a competition whose winner is obvious from the start
Ferrari's badge is a prancing horse, so a race named after it could be a horse race of a particular kind

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the fanciful second reading: a motor race named for Ferrari's single-horse emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse race is an idiom for a contest with only one realistic winner.

clue.text: Mimic boy dressed in Roman style

a son is a boy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' here means a formal title, not fashion.

clue.text: Those checking reports of prospective partners drinking in bed

taken as written

clue.text: Advice to visit a S American plain or plateau

cut short, the word loses its last letter

clue.text: Speculates or introspects at first in academic papers

clue.text: A warehouse robbed of Old Master

clue.text: Support publicity work

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity work
op is short for opus, a work

clue.text: Propose to maiden on return, clutching ring

the pair of pieces is read back to front

parts.note: taken as written
O is ring-shaped
